headlines.title: Stockton woman among 3 killed in mass shooting at new Idaho In-N-Out
headlines.description: A 23-year-old Stockton woman who dreamed of one day managing an In-N-Out Burger was among three people killed in a mass shooting at a newly opened location in Idaho, her family confirmed. Ashley Garibay, described by her family as a devoted daughter, sister, auntie, and friend, had traveled to the new Idaho restaurant to help with its opening. The location had opened just days before the shooting rampage on Saturday. Garibay worked at an In-N-Out in Stockton, employees confirmed to Sacramento NBC affiliate KCRA. Her family said she would proudly travel to open new stores to pursue her dream of management. In a statement, Garibay’s family said she had a “beautiful soul” and “loved living life.” “She was adventurous, outgoing, smart and driven, never letting obstacles get in her way,” the family statement read. The family expressed gratitude to the In-N-Out associates, first responders, and bystanders who rushed to Garibay’s aid to comfort her in her final moments. They have launched an online fundraiser to help cover funeral expenses, calling her an “In-N-Out All-Star” who left a lasting impression on many souls. The news has devastated the Stockton community. “It’s really sad, I’m thinking that I may have even known or ran into this young lady because I used to work around this area,” Stockton resident Memo Ramirez Sr. said. “It’s really sad to know that there’s a family in mourning right now, that their baby girl isn’t coming home.” The shooting left three people dead and seven others injured. Hundreds of customers were present to witness the terror. Klen Kurby, a pastor who was inside the restaurant getting ready to leave when the gunfire erupted, described the chaotic scene. “We were just in a sea of panic, and there were hundreds of people around there in the restaurant coming, leaving the restaurant and so on. Literally hundreds of people,” Kurby said. “And we were just mainly running for our lives. And we could tell by the sound. And some of it was like not just single shots, like an automatic weapon, but we ran.” In-N-Out’s owner released a statement mourning the victims: “He took the precious lives of our associate and customers, innocent people who never saw it coming.” Police are crediting two good Samaritans — an off-duty state trooper and a man seen confronting the shooter in the drive-thru — with saving lives through their heroic actions. “We believe their actions helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties,” Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said. The shooter reportedly died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

headlines.title: Pittsburg residents protest approved data center, demand halt to development
headlines.description: The future of a planned data center is once again taking center stage in Pittsburg as residents demanding a halt to the controversial development rallied outside City Hall. Dozens of residents gathered ahead of a City Council meeting dedicated entirely to the project, searching for answers from the city and action to stop the already approved data center. The data center was approved in 2024. AVAIO Digital plans to build the facility at the former Delta View Golf Course, which is part of the city’s planned technology park. City leaders say the project will create jobs, generate tax revenue, and help turn the site into a technology hub. But opponents argue they still lack a clear picture of the impacts. “There’s too many unknowns,” Pittsburg resident Mark Linde said. “I want to see the finances, I want to see more of the situation of how the water is going to actually work, how the electricity is going to work, how the power purchase is going to work, what the citizens are getting if there is no way out. But at this point, we want it stopped.” Residents also raised concerns about transparency from the city, noise from backup generators, and air quality. Amhari Perkins, who lives about a mile from the proposed site, worries about pollution. “We are already in a pretty working-class community, low income as some may say, and not at the highest of the chart when it comes to health,” Perkins said. “Just know this has been approved and going to be coming so close to our homes, a lot of us already are dealing with health issues.” City leaders say the project has completed its environmental review and will use air cooling and mostly recycled water. However, residents claim that despite the project already getting approval, many people just found out about it — sparking protests and a petition. “They are trying to [do] this behind our backs. Nobody knew anything until a month or two ago,” resident Alma Rodriguez said. The City Council meeting is expected to focus entirely on data centers. The city declined an interview before the meeting, stating that officials will answer questions afterward. Meanwhile, opponents say they are still hoping to keep shovels out of the ground. “All I can do is fight, that’s all the community can do is fight, and hopefully we get answers tonight,” Perkins said.

headlines.title: Bay Area scammers prey on distraught pet owners with fake veterinary emergencies
headlines.description: A heartbreaking situation for Bay Area pet owners is being exploited by scammers who target distraught families searching for their missing animals. The scammers pretend to be from veterinary hospitals and attempt to convince people to shell out thousands of dollars to save their pets. Now, one San Jose family is speaking out to warn others. It all started on July 1 when the Nottingham family’s 8-year-old cat, Tylette, went missing. “She’s my little cuddle bug, I miss her every day,” Madison Nottingham said. Madison Nottingham and her mother, Bobbie Nottingham, put up more than 300 fliers in their neighborhood and posted an online plea for help finding their cat. Weeks later, they received a call from a man who said he was at a San Jose veterinary hospital with Tylette. He even gave the name of a woman who he claimed brought the cat in after it had been hit by a car, offering specific medical details. “The cat is sedated and is immobilized,” Bobbie Nottingham said. “I asked what type of surgery did she need, he said spinal alignment and broken femur and she’d need surgery immediately.” Bobbie Nottingham said the man told her the operation would cost more than $2,700. Suspicious, she called the veterinary hospital directly and learned her cat was not there. “Pretty shocked that someone would prey on our grief and on our fears,” Bobbie Nottingham said. The Nottinghams aren’t the only ones being targeted. Rebekah Davis-Matthews, the founder of Lost and Found Pets of Santa Clara County, says this type of deception is common, and scammers are now turning to artificial intelligence to pull it off. “If they have a picture of your pet, because you posted it, they can always alter it with AI to make it look like they have your animal,” Davis-Matthews said. She also warned of another common tactic. “There’s these people who say they have drones and will help you search for the animal and they demand payment up front, but there’s no search. They are just trying to scam money from people,” Davis-Matthews said. While the Nottinghams did not give the scammer any money, they spoke to other pet owners who unfortunately did. “You are so hopeful. You want to believe anyone who has your cat,” Madison Nottingham said. The search for Tylette continues, and the family has added a $500 reward, hoping to be reunited with their beloved pet.

headlines.title: San Francisco sees surge in all-cash home sales driven by AI boom
headlines.description: Paying cash for a home isn’t too unusual in some markets, but in San Francisco — a city known for multimillion-dollar properties — paying cash used to be rare. That is no longer the case. A red-hot housing market is driving a surge in all-cash offers. According to data from Redfin, 30% of all home sales in the San Francisco Bay Area market from April through June were cash transactions. That is a significant change from 2021, when less than 20% of sales were for cash. Currently, cash sales in the region are slightly higher than the national average. In Noe Valley, one of the city’s most sought-after neighborhoods for families, homes listed by Compass Realty agent James Rowbotham and his sister, Zara, are being snapped up fast in cash — even with price tags of $5 million to $6 million. Rowbotham said they sold a similar nearby home a few months ago. “It was a couple that bought the house. And that was all cash. That was a cash buy, but just the two of them for seven bed, seven bath,” Rowbotham said. In the past, most buyers couldn’t come up with that much money on the spot. But with San Francisco’s continued surge of artificial intelligence money into the local economy and housing inventory that continues to be tight, prices in the city are rising, along with the number of cash sales. However, not everyone is cashing in AI stock to make those offers. Dan Risman Jones of Ascend Real Estate noted that family wealth is also a factor. “I have one transaction right now; parents are purchasing the property for the kids using all cash. I assumed that at some point the kids will get loans for it, for the property,” Risman Jones said. According to Rowbotham, San Francisco is once again a prime destination. People who moved to cities in Texas or Florida during the pandemic are now trying to return, and being the epicenter of the AI economy is part of that draw. “The city is booming. It’s on fire. And I don’t see it going down anytime soon because of the location, the weather, the people,” Rowbotham said. Rowbotham and Risman Jones both acknowledge that competing against a cash offer can be intimidating for buyers. But they note there are strategies they have used to help their clients beat out cash offers, recommending that buyers be prepared to be flexible and find real estate agents who know the market well.

headlines.title: 6-alarm fire destroys dozens of Foster City condos, displaces families
headlines.description: A major cleanup is underway in Foster City, bringing big questions for displaced families after a six-alarm fire tore through dozens of condominiums. The blaze at Spinnaker Cove sparked Sunday afternoon and raged for nearly nine hours. Four firefighters were injured but are expected to be OK. Everyone was rescued, but the building — which was built in the 1980s and, according to residents, had no sprinklers — continues to fall apart. “We see fire and smoke … inside my home … so I go outside … And scream ‘help,’” one resident recalled. Firefighters remain on the scene monitoring for hot spots. While crews know the general origin of the fire, investigators say it will be a while before they can confirm exactly how it started. Residents left with nothing, searching for missing pets It will be a while before residents can assess the damage themselves. Yasmin Bishop was out of town when the fire started and received a photo showing her first-floor condo bulging from water damage. She suspects all her belongings are gone. “It’s horrible. Literally everything I own is in my unit and I may not even be able to go in and retrieve any of it,” Bishop said. “It’s really awful to have to start over with nothing.” While human residents safely escaped, some families are now desperate to find their pets. Bishop is posting fliers hoping to locate her two cats, Felix and Eloise. At least one other neighbor is also missing two cats. “They’re actually my daughters’ cats, they named them and they’re really precious to them and so it’s just heartbreaking you know,” Bishop said. “We just adore them so much.” Community steps up to help victims Residents are receiving help in the recovery process. A Red Cross shelter was opened nearby, and the Foster City Chamber of Commerce and Foundation is raising money for the victims, aiming for a minimum of $1,000 for each of the 51 units that perished. “There’s a lot of clothing needs right now. Essential items, underwear, socks, that kind of thing. There’s back-to-school items because there are kids that were supposed to be starting school next week, and then eventually that’s going to turn into replacement items for housing,” said Crystal Tilton with the Foster City Chamber of Commerce and Foundation. Insurance experts urge documentation For those who are insured, experts recommend keeping all receipts for meals or hotel stays, as they could be covered depending on the policy. Karen Collins of the American Property Casualty Insurance Association also shared a warning for anyone watching the devastation unfold. “Before you have the loss, go in and document what’s in your house so if everything is lost you can have a much more smooth recovery process on what needs to get reimbursed under the personal property section of your policy,” Collins said. NBC Bay Area’s Gia Vang has more in the video report above.

headlines.title: Inside look at new shark-tracking technology
headlines.description: New technology will help track sharks from the water and the air. The goal is to keep the water safe for triathletes competing in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics as well as Bay Area surfers. The technology comes in the form of a 10-foot-long device that goes into the water. It is solar powered with sensors that relay information to lifeguards on the beach. Drones on board will also be launched into the air to fly around and locate sharks. The technology was developed at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB), close to where the Olympics will be held. Triathletes will be swimming in Long Beach harbor, which is known to have sharks nearby. The technology is expected to be used in Bay Area waters soon, helping lifeguards answer questions people have about shark behavior. “Like where are all these sharks coming from, what are they doing here, when are they gonna leave? Now with all this technology, we can start to really address those questions,” CSULB Shark Lab Director Dr. Chris Lowe said.

headlines.title: California Prop 39: Voter ID on the ballot in November
headlines.description: California voters in November will decide whether to require people to show identification at the polls. If Proposition 39 passes, California voters would need to provide a government-issued ID at the polls or the last four digits of a government-issued identification number when voting by mail. Reform California is the group behind the proposition and led by Republican State Assemblymember Carl DeMaio. DeMaio said the measure would tighten election rules through verified citizenship and a report from election officials each year. “We believe that people should continue to have convenience for voting and make voting easy,” DeMaio said. “But we do require identification. You can do that with a multitude of government IDs and for mail-in ballots just the last four digits.” On the other hand, Common Cause California opposes Prop 39, saying the measure would make it harder to vote. “Prop 39 does not lay out any sort of guidelines on how we, for example, cure ballots. That’s how do we correct issues such as signatures or maybe wrong digit placements for verification numbers,” Common Cause California Executive Director Darius Kemp said. “It doesn’t do any of that.” Some voters resonated with Kemp, especially once they learned more about the proposition. A University of California, Berkely poll conducted in April found 56% of respondents initially supported the measure. After they understood the measure’s political context, the support dropped to 39%. “I’m probably indifferent to be honest,” voter Muhammad Joyo said. “I can see why people wouldn’t like that. I can also see why people would want that.”

headlines.title: Giants trade left-handed starting pitcher Robbie Ray to Padres for two prospects
headlines.description: The Giants parted with one of their two ace-caliber starting pitchers. San Francisco traded left-handed pitcher Robbie Ray to the San Diego Padres on Monday, the team announced after ESPN’s Jeff Passan first reported the news. The Giants received right-handed pitching prospect Miguel Mendez and shortstop prospect Joniel Hernandez from San Diego. The 24-year-old Mendez was the Padres’ No. 4 prospect, according to MLB.com, and in 12 combined starts across the High-A and Double-A levels this season, posted a 4.79 ERA with 39 strikeouts and 17 walks in 35 2/3 innings pitched. Hernandez, 17, was San Diego’s No. 9 prospect, and batted .303/.424/.503 with four home runs and 43 RBI in 155 at-bats in rookie ball. Since his June 16 outing, Ray has been one of MLB’s best starters, posting a 1.65 ERA and 61 strikeouts in 60 innings. In his final Giants start against the San Diego Padres on Thursday at Petco Park, Ray allowed four hits and one earned run while striking out six in six dominant innings. “I tried to put everything out of my head leading up to this start, but yeah, it obviously comes up now that this could be my last start in a Giants uniform,” Ray said following Thursday’s outing. San Francisco originally acquired Ray in a trade with the Seattle Mariners in Jan. 2024 as the former Cy Young Award winner was rehabbing from Tommy John surgery. Ray eventually debuted with the Giants on July 24 of that year, making seven starts before the season ended. A fully healthy Ray then returned to Cy Young form in the first half of the 2025 MLB season, earning his second All-Star nod, before trailing off toward the end of the campaign. In 61 appearances (60 starts) across three seasons with San Francisco, Ray posted a combined 3.54 ERA with 336 strikeouts and 145 walks across 335 2/3 innings pitched. He now will join righty Michael King atop the the Padres’ starting rotation, while two intriguing prospects join a rising Giants farm system. Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast

headlines.title: Giants trade Luis Arraez, Caleb Kilian to Phillies for two pitching prospects
headlines.description: The Giants made a difficult, yet expected move. San Francisco traded All-Star second baseman Luis Arraez and relief pitcher Caleb Kilian to the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday, the team announced after ESPN’s Jeff Passan and The Athletic’s Jayson Stark first reported the news. The Giants received pitching prospects Ramon Marquez and Marty Gair in the deal with the Phillies. San Francisco signed Arraez to a one-year, $12 million free-agent contract last offseason. Despite initial concerns regarding the veteran second baseman’s defense, Arraez quickly proved to be a more than serviceable defender at the position after working with Giants infield coach Ron Washington. However, his biggest impact throughout the first half of the 2026 MLB season was with the bat. In 105 games with San Francisco before the trade, Arraez batted .324/.360/.440 with four home runs, 43 RBI and 10 stolen bases, earning him his fourth career All-Star nod. With Arraez on the move and Casey Schmitt on the injured list with a torn left meniscus, the Giants likely will use Christian Koss and Osleivis Basabe at second base. San Francisco might not be done making moves, either. Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast

headlines.title: San Francisco Firebells pick up first win of the season
headlines.description: San Francisco’s women’s professional baseball team made history Sunday after winning its first game of the season. The Firebells opened their inaugural season with a 11-3 victory over the Boston Hunters. The win came one day after the league’s first ever game with the Los Angeles Queens versus the New York Heights. Kelsie Whitmore, the No. 1 overall pick, helped lead the way in the franchise’s debut. “I know this is just game one. We have a long season ahead. The goal is to keep the energy that we have, the momentum. Love the squad that we’re on, just keep it going,” Whitmore said. The Firebells will face off against the Heights on Thursday and the Queens on Friday.

headlines.title: 5 men arrested by Walnut Creek police in online child sex crime sting
headlines.description: Four men from across the Bay Area and one visiting from Europe were arrested by Walnut Creek police this week for allegedly traveling to the city to meet up with children for sexual exploitation. The Walnut Creek Police Department in conjunction with the Contra Costa County Crimes Against Children Task Force targeted adults using social media to target children. According to police, five men are now facing allegations of attempted lewd acts with a minor, contacting a minor to commit a sex offense, and arranging to meet a minor for sex. Arrested were Concord resident Andrew Garcia, 32, Antioch resident Billie Ray Breland, 29, and Taesu Park, 36, from Marin County. A man visiting from Germany was also arrested, Rudolf Naused Robl, 42, and a Walnut Creek resident, Jacek Markiewicz, 76, was also arrested on suspicion of attempted kidnapping.

headlines.title: Bystanders resuscitate teen at San Mateo County beach
headlines.description: Good Samaritans resuscitated a teenager who appeared to have drowned at San Gregorio State Beach in San Mateo County on Sunday, according to Cal Fire. First responders were called to the beach south of Half Moon Bay on a report of an 18-year-old found unconscious in the lagoon area, Cal Fire said. Authorities believe the person had been submerged in water for a minimum of two minutes and was found unresponsive and not breathing. “Thanks to the immediate action of quick-thinking bystanders who called 911 and started early Bystander CPR, the patient regained breathing and consciousness prior to the arrival of first responders,” Cal Fire said. Multiple agencies arrived at the scene and the patient was transported to the hospital, where they were reported in stable condition.
